audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Volibear's stun 'E Frenzied Maul'. Both halves are wrong: Frenzied Maul is his W (5s, on-hit, heals on the second stack) and it has no CC; his E is Sky Splitter (16s, slow plus a self-shield). The stun belongs to Q Thundering Smash (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s), which is also an auto-attack reset. Wrong in spikes[3].text, mid, and wants.foe[0].
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon: Q Thundering Smash (hardCC, autoReset), W Frenzied Maul (heal, onHit), E Sky Splitter (slow, shield, zone). A player told to dodge an 'E stun' will watch the wrong ability and eat the real one.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash (Q) is the stun and it is an auto-reset — his wind-up, not the cast, is your cue. Frenzied Maul is the W bite that heals him on the second application.

audit.whatIsWrong: early contains the duplicated fragment 'His Ki Barrier Ki Barrier shield eats the return damage'.
audit.why: Straight text defect that reads as broken generation on a paid page.
audit.corrected: His Ki Barrier shield eats the return damage.

audit.why: Both layers agree row for row (Skill/Shen/Shen/Skill/Skill/Shen/Shen). Shape is defensible against a 57.43 Shen win rate: Volibear contests at 4-6 when Frenzied Maul healing and his R dive come online, Shen owns the 2-3 pattern window and both item stages.

Four spikes present: Lvl 2-3 (Shadow Dash + Spirit's Refuge), Lvl 6 (Stand United vs his telegraphed R), 1st item (anti-heal), and an enemy spike. Anti-heal is correctly flagged as the item priority — Frenzied Maul is his only sustain.
Both packet suspectNames ('Use Stand United', "Thundering Smash's") are FALSE POSITIVES — both match the kit files exactly. The real name error was elsewhere and the packet did not flag it.

edits.before: Volibear's E Frenzied Maul stun is his biggest threat window before you have anti-heal — don't let him land it and his W in the same combo or he out-trades your Ki Barrier shield.
edits.after: Volibear's Q Thundering Smash stun is his biggest threat window before you have anti-heal — don't let it land into two Frenzied Maul bites or he out-trades your Ki Barrier shield.

edits.before: Land E Frenzied Maul stun into W-bite before your W zone is placed so he trades without auto-block
edits.after: Land the Q Thundering Smash stun into a double Frenzied Maul bite before your W zone is down

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are about maintaining the lead without getting stunned — his E Frenzied Maul stun is dangerous if he lands it before you drop W, so always have your blade positioned between you. Trade only when his Q Thundering Smash is on cooldown so he can't dash through your W zone unexpectedly. At Level 6 the lane becomes your playground: Stand United makes every fight on the map a potential 2v1 for the enemy. When Volibear presses his R to kill a tower, track it and ask whether you should Stand United onto the target he's diving — his ult is loud, it telegraphs, and cancelling a Volibear dive with a global shield and instant TP is exactly what this kit is built for. By now your anti-heal item should be online or nearly complete; without it his W bite passive healing lets him sustain through your trades, so prioritize it before any second tank item.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are about maintaining the lead without getting stunned — his Q Thundering Smash stun is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is your cue, not the cast. Trade only while that 12-second Q is down so he can't dash through your W zone unexpectedly. At Level 6 the lane becomes your playground: Stand United makes every fight on the map a potential 2v1 for the enemy. When Volibear presses his R to kill a tower, track it and ask whether you should Stand United onto the target he's diving — his ult is loud, it telegraphs, and cancelling a Volibear dive with a global shield and instant TP is exactly what this kit is built for. By now your anti-heal item should be online or nearly complete; without it his Frenzied Maul healing lets him sustain through your trades, so prioritize it before any second tank item.

edits.before: At Level 1 respect his raw auto damage — Volibear's passive stacks give him surprising burst if you stand in his face without your taunt ready. Farm safely and don't trade until you have E. Level 2 changes everything: the moment you unlock Shadow Dash, step up and force a short trade — E into him so his autos must target you, drop W behind you so his Q dash or W-bite autos are all blocked by Spirit's Refuge, then fire Q through the blade for empowered magic damage. His Ki Barrier Ki Barrier shield eats the return damage and you come out clearly ahead. Level 3 is your clearest window: with Q, W, and E all online you can bait his Q Thundering Smash dash, E-taunt into him, place W so the blade is between you and him, and Q through it — that three-ability combo with the Ki Barrier shield takes a large chunk of his health before his W passive healing does anything meaningful.
edits.after: At Level 1 respect his raw auto damage — Volibear's passive stacks give him surprising burst if you stand in his face without your taunt ready. Your Ki Barrier shield eats the return damage and you come out clearly ahead. Level 3 is your clearest window: with Q, W, and E all online you can bait his Q Thundering Smash dash, E-taunt into him, place W so the blade is between you and him, and Q through it — that three-ability combo with the Ki Barrier shield takes a large chunk of his health before Frenzied Maul's healing does anything meaningful.

notes: The packet's two suspectNames were both false positives, while the genuine fabrication — 'E Frenzied Maul stun', which merges his W's name onto his E's slot and attaches his Q's CC — went unflagged in three fields. Also fixed the duplicated 'Ki Barrier Ki Barrier' fragment in early.
